The Court Made The Following:
 Order

This writ petition is filed seeking for following reliefs:
(a) Issue a writ of certiorari quashing the general award dated 20.04.2017 passed by the respondent no.3 in No.KIADB:LAQ:95: 2017-18 which is produced at Annexure-H to the writ petition in so far petitioner's land bearing Sy.No.29/5,
measuring 0.9 guntas and general award dated 31.12.2013 passed by the respondent no.3 in No.KIADB:LAQ: 2013-14 which is produced at Annexure-J to the writ petition in so far petitioner's land bearing Sy.No.204/1, measuring 0.10 guntas at Bannikuppe village, Harohalli hobli, Harohalli taluk, Ramanagar is concerned.

sentences.text:
2 (b) Issue any suitable order, direction or writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents herein to consider the case of the petitioner as per Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act or in the allotment of developed land, etc.,
2.

Smt. Latha S.S., learned counsel for petitioners submitted that late petitioners were absolute owners of land bearing Sy.no.29/5, measuring 0.9 guntas and land bearing Sy.no.204/1, measuring 0.10 guntas of land situated at Bannikuppe village, Horahalli hobli, Harohalli taluk, Bangalore Rural District (referred to as 'petition schedule property').
Respondent no.2 acquired said lands for formation of industrial area under preliminary notification dated 25.10.2006, and final notification dated 29.01.2010.

3. It was submitted that though petitioners were entitled to higher compensation under consent award, without offering opportunity to avail same, General Award was passed by Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO), which was under challenge.
It was submitted that under similar circumstances, this Court allowed W.P.nos.16642-649/2012 (Sri. C.V.Krisnareddy & Others v. The State of Karnataka and Others) vide order 22.06.2012.

entities.text: C.V.Krisnareddy & Others v. The State of Karnataka and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Relying upon same, sought for granting similar relief.

On other hand, Sri Manjunath V. Rayappa, learned AGA, for respondent no.1 and Sri K. Vasanth,
learned counsel for respondents no.2 and 3 submitted that, in case, petitioners furnish relevant documents such as title deeds etc., along with representation, same would be considered in accordance with law, within reasonable time.

5. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.
6.
From above, it is seen that failure to pass consent award is due to non-furnishing of application along with supporting documents like title deeds etc. by petitioners.

In view orders passed in W.P.nos.16642-649/2012 (supra), and several matters, this Court under similar circumstances had quashed General Award and directed respondents to consider petitioner's case for passing consent award.
Said decision would squarely apply in this case also.
7. Accordingly, Writ petition is disposed of.

Impugned General Awards dated 20.04.2017 bearing no.KIADB:LAQ:95:
2017-18 (Annexure-H) and no.KIADB:LAQ:2013-14 (Annexure-J) dated 31.12.2013 passed by respondent no.3 in NC: 2023:KHC:41056 respect of land bearing Sy.no.29/5, measuring 0.9 guntas and Sy.no.204/1, measuring 0.10 guntas respectively, situated at Bannikuppe village, Harohalli hobli, Harohalli taluk,
Ramanagar, insofar as petitioners' land is concerned.
